artifacts.summary: All 8 phases completed: fixed Create Mode's topic-assignment order and AskUserQuestion schema, and extracted task-type detection into a tested strong-anchor/weak-signal library, removing literature's erroneous keyword_overrides. Deployed and confirmed end-to-end.

completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed /task Create Mode's topic-assignment ordering defect (manage-topics.sh set now runs after the task exists, never before) and its AskUserQuestion schema, and replaced task-type detection's first-match-wins keyword table with a shared, tested strong-anchor + weak-signal-threshold library that also closes the literature-keyword-overrides false-positive. Both new fixture suites pass from the deployed copy; redeployed and verified end-to-end against a fresh scratch state.json.

memory_candidates.content: A keyword_overrides key in an extension manifest.json IS the resolved task_type verbatim -- it is never remapped or validated against the extension's own routing table. An extension with routing_exempt: true and no .routing block must therefore never declare keyword_overrides at all: the resolved key would be a task_type no routing consumer (command-route-skill.sh, command-route-agent.sh) can dispatch, which is a worse failure than not matching early. Check this before adding keyword_overrides to any new extension manifest, and check every existing manifest's key against its own task_type/.routing block when auditing this class of defect.

For a shell script whose PROJECT_ROOT/SCRIPT_DIR resolution is relative to its OWN file location (not overridable by env var), a fixture-driven test suite must copy the real script (and its lib/ dependencies) into a mktemp -d scratch repo shaped like the real deploy target (.claude/scripts/{,lib/} + specs/state.json), then invoke the COPY -- never the live script pointed at a fixture path. See build_fixture_repo() in test-skill-base-lifecycle.sh (the canonical precedent) and its reuse in test-manage-topics-create-order.sh. This is required whenever the script under test resolves its own root via `cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd` rather than accepting an override argument.

When replacing a first-keyword-match-wins routing table (prone to single-common-word false positives like "agent", "proof", "lean" appearing in passing), a strong-anchor + weak-signal-threshold rule is an effective middle ground: (1) a short list of high-confidence multi-word phrases or structural patterns (file paths, hyphenated compounds, leading slash-commands) resolves immediately; (2) everything else accumulates a per-candidate-type count of DISTINCT weak keyword matches and only resolves at a threshold (>=2 worked well here) with ties broken by declaration order. This is worth a dedicated fixture suite asserting both the false positives it fixes AND the true positives it must not break (the same description class that motivated the original single-keyword rule).
